stem: Preferred decalcifier for an IHC/ISH-heavy bone specimen:
rationale: EDTA is slower but generally preserves antigens and nucleic acids better than strong mineral acids.

distractor_rationales.A: Concentrated nitric acid decalcifies rapidly but can damage morphology, antigens, and nucleic acids.
distractor_rationales.B: Unvalidated hydrochloric acid may impair IHC and ISH targets and is not the preferred choice here.
distractor_rationales.C: Picric acid is not the routine preferred decalcifier when preservation of antigens and nucleic acids is the priority.

learning_objective: Select a decalcification method that better preserves antigens and nucleic acids for IHC and ISH.
